Senses.PreferredTarget: The udumbara flower is blooming; its pure fragrance comes without end.

Occurrences.Kwic: 天童叔翁上山下曉老和尚為雲南恒秀法姪掃南山先老和尚祖塔，請上堂。「佛佛授手、祖祖傳持，開鑿人天眼目、挽回上古風規。此乃我密祖崛起太白、勒轉滹沱時之機用，普天匝地緇流莫不遭其塗毒、受其噓吹。然克紹嫡傳，秖獲二六真種，茲馳瓣香，遠供塔頭，即法伯雙桂老人之嫡孫恒秀林公也。能於滇黔繩其祖武，飲水知源，難忘木本，不遠萬里虔齎淨資，恭啟山僧向人天眾前為伊拈出。」驀豎拂子云：「大眾！且道拈出後如何？優曇花正開，清香來不徹。」擲拂子，下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB355.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hengxiulin of Lülüo. The first speaker is Shanxiao of Tiantong, the guest teacher named in the record's heading. He speaks for a distant offering associated with Hengxiu of Yunnan at an ancestral pagoda service. His address recalls the transmission through their elders, says only a few true seeds inherited it, and praises remembering the source when drinking water and the root of a tree despite great distance. Raising his whisk, he asks what happens after it has been brought forth and answers with the blooming udumbara and pure fragrance coming without end. He throws down the whisk and leaves. The image gives this lineage remembrance and offering a present flowering; it does not document an actual plant flowering at the pagoda. The headword is rendered: The udumbara flower is blooming; its pure fragrance comes without end.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：雨不來，旱彌烈。草木枯，金石裂。江流斷，井泉竭。盡大地，生意絕。東湖上，乾坤別。最清涼，無惱熱。優曇花正開，清香來不徹。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1372.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wuwen Daocan. Wuwen Daocan begins with the opposite of flourishing: no rain, worsening drought, withered plants, cracked stone and metal, dried rivers and wells, and vitality cut off across the earth. He then says the world at East Lake is different, completely cool and free of distressing heat, and closes with the udumbara in bloom and fragrance coming without end. The flower is the culminating image of that contrast between desiccation and inexhaustible freshness. The address records neither the arrival of physical rain nor a timetable for a rare flower; those outcomes should not be added to the saying. The headword is rendered: The udumbara flower is blooming; its pure fragrance comes without end.

Entries.SourceTerm: 堪報不報之恩，共助無為之化

Senses.PreferredTarget: Repay the kindness that cannot be repaid, and together aid a transformation free of contrivance.
AlternateTargets: Answer the unrepayable debt of kindness and help the work of effortless change.
SearchAliases: repay unrepayable kindness aid effortless transformation Chan
Senses.Note: Feiyin says the pair while challenging his retreat assembly, and Yinyuan applies it to a person who can move freely through everyday affairs. Dabian and Zixian bring it into their own talks on guidance and restoring a seat. Yuanan uses it in an address on recognition, Huiyue in an opening-hall gathering, and Yushan after a critique of inherited verse. The first debt is called unrepayable because its kindness exceeds a simple return; the second clause speaks of shared transformation without forced manipulation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：「誰是其人？」僧一喝，師便打，乃云：「天寒地寒，大家在者裏，風和陽和，彼此行物外，有佛處不得住，沒孔鐵鎚恐虫蛀，無佛處急走過，枯木巖前蹉路多，恁麼不去也，驀地翻身尋本據。摘楊花，摘楊花，誰憶趙州老作家，然則金粟今朝解制，還是去的是？不去的是？把住兩頭咸踢脫，等閒舉步廓周沙。」下座。廣東僧悅西請上堂，師云：「千鄉萬里來，單為個一著，須要自回光，不用多行腳，江北江南共天日，海東海西同風月，青山綠水古猶今，翠竹黃花明且灼，回頭便是故家鄉，當體無羈本寥廓。」以拄杖卓一卓云：「還會麼？」便下座。開爐上堂，問：「有一人呼喚不回頭，點即不到；有一人長年不出戶，到即不點。未審恁麼人如何？」師云：「七縱八橫。」進云：「恁麼則解拈一粒粟供養于此人去也。」師云：「清風生腋下。」進云：「龍得水時添意氣，虎逢山色長威獰。」師打云：「雲雷相送。」乃云：「逐歲開爐枉費工夫，長年結制分明鈍置，若是過量底人聞恁麼道，便乃掀倒禪床、喝散大眾，把山僧爛椎一頓，堪報不報之恩，共助無為之化；其或未然，不免向第二門頭放一線道，烹佛烹祖大爐鞴，煆生煆死惡鉗鎚，四海英靈奇衲子，到來都與痛加錐，不惟覿面提持，抑顯格外風規，泥牛入海人皆會，金佛度爐若個知。」驀拈拄杖，云：「拄杖子吞卻乾坤了也，是汝諸人更向何處出氣？若云火燄為三世諸佛說法，正是熟睡饒寱語，三世諸佛立地聽，也是杓卜聽虛聲。到者裏，若存纖毫異見，即墮鐵圍那邊。正恁麼時，金佛度爐一句作麼生道？毛吞巨海尋常事，芥納須彌匹似閑。」下座。上堂，舉：「《楞嚴經》佛告阿難云：『吾不見時，何不見吾不見之處，若見不見，自然非彼不見之相，若不見吾不見之地，自然非物，云何非汝。』」師云：「大小世尊為阿難牽來拽去，到末梢頭直得鉤繩自斷，令他覿體全彰、脫灑自繇，不假風帆孤舟到岸。所以當時遠祖白雲端禪師作頌發明其意，云：『堂前露柱久懷胎，生下孩兒頗俊哉，未解語言先作賦，一操直取狀元來。』蓋遠祖之意，正古人所謂『若欲播揚大教，須從自己胸襟中流出將來，與我蓋天蓋地。』一期語句不妨奇怪，山僧今日因求嗣上堂，亦有一頌，不惟幾百年後與遠祖鬥富，亦令現前一切人天凡有所願悉皆如意。頌曰：『天曉園林盡放花，十分春色最交加，人多賞翫渾如醉，得意忘歸到月斜。』」卓拄杖，下座。伯載吳居士將逝，遺囑請上堂，

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：「三喝、四喝後又作麼生？」僧遂歸眾。問：「昔日寶壽開堂，三聖推出一僧，壽便打，意旨如何？」師云：「正令當行。」進云：「既然如是，因甚三聖又道：『瞎卻鎮州一城人眼去在？』」師云：「疑殺天下人。」進云：「今日新靈峰陞座，也不用棒、也不瞎卻人眼，畢竟將何為人？」師云：「一句迥開三要印，爍迦眼出透金塵。」進云：「人平不語，水平不流。」師云：「賴得闍黎領話。」僧便喝，師便打，乃云：「十方同聚會，明明古佛家風；遍界絕遮攔，處處祖師巴鼻。樓閣雲中僧世界，栴檀海岸老叢林，金風起而枯木龍吟，霜葉凋而寒嵒華散。林間鳥語共唱無生，嶺上猿聲深譚般若，落落風清三佛地，溶溶月朗四明州。直得人人頂門上輝大寶光，各各腳跟下縱橫十字，果是超方作者，豁開正眼圓明，便乃透過百匝千重，不妨任意橫三豎四。如是，則念念靈山出世，步步兜率下生，分別現曼殊之心，運用動普賢之行，頭頭引歸寶所，味味盡是醍醐，然後以金剛劍剪除異見稠林，斷貫索穿盡衲僧鼻孔，梯航三有，津濟四生，堪報不報之恩，共助無為之化。正當恁麼時，流通正脈、扶豎綱宗一句又作麼生道？寶藏撥開於此日，千燈五葉轉光新。」復舉：「興化和尚云：『三聖道：「逢人即不出，出則便為人。」興化則不然，逢人即出，出則不為人。』雪嵒欽云：『二大老所謂一條拄杖兩人舁，被天寧拗作兩橛了也。』以拄杖倚左邊，云：『且聽各自平分。』」師云：「欽祖幸然拗折，今日不肖兒孫未免更將鸞膠為伊續起，逢人即出、逢人不出，兩彩一賽，如箭中的。金鳳銜華下彩樓，眼裏瞳人吹觱栗，三臺須是大家催，無限清風生八極。」白椎，云：「諦觀法王法，法王法如是。」卓拄杖一下，下座。勉參。「靈峰寺裏開爐，炭墼家常儘有，更賴現前兄弟，竭力同心出手。輕輕撥動火柴頭，烈燄亙天射牛斗，冷灰豆爆忽雷轟，叢林盡作師子吼。斷送生蛇化活龍，差排古佛離窠臼，無賓主句火爐頭，笑他趙老揚家醜。後來雪嵒欽又云：『不冷不熱爐鞴，半真半假金鋀，鑄作缾盤釵釧，卻成品字柴頭。』且道：與趙州無賓主話相去多少？若向者裏緇素得出，二大老性命在諸仁手裏；若緇素不出，諸仁性命卻在山僧手裏。」卓拄杖，云：「還委悉麼？莫向白雲深處坐，好看千嶂起風雷。」開爐，上堂。「烹佛烹祖大爐鞴，量等虛空包法界；煆凡煆聖惡鉗錘，千手大悲亦皺眉。鈍銕頑銅銷爍盡，精金美玉轉新奇，烈燄不

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 師云：「三喝、四喝後又作麼生？」僧遂歸眾。問：「昔日寶壽開堂，三聖推出一僧，壽便打，意旨如何？」師云：「正令當行。」進云：「既然如是，因甚三聖又道：『瞎卻鎮州一城人眼去在？』」師云：「疑殺天下人。」進云：「今日新靈峰陞座，也不用棒、也不瞎卻人眼，畢竟將何為人？」師云：「一句迥開三要印，爍迦眼出透金塵。」進云：「人平不語，水平不流。」師云：「賴得闍黎領話。」僧便喝，師便打，乃云：「十方同聚會，明明古佛家風；遍界絕遮攔，處處祖師巴鼻。樓閣雲中僧世界，栴檀海岸老叢林，金風起而枯木龍吟，霜葉凋而寒嵒華散。林間鳥語共唱無生，嶺上猿聲深譚般若，落落風清三佛地，溶溶月朗四明州。直得人人頂門上輝大寶光，各各腳跟下縱橫十字，果是超方作者，豁開正眼圓明，便乃透過百匝千重，不妨任意橫三豎四。如是，則念念靈山出世，步步兜率下生，分別現曼殊之心，運用動普賢之行，頭頭引歸寶所，味味盡是醍醐，然後以金剛劍剪除異見稠林，斷貫索穿盡衲僧鼻孔，梯航三有，津濟四生，堪報不報之恩，共助無為之化。正當恁麼時，流通正脈、扶豎綱宗一句又作麼生道？寶藏撥開於此日，千燈五葉轉光新。」復舉：「興化和尚云：『三聖道：「逢人即不出，出則便為人。」興化則不然，逢人即出，出則不為人。』雪嵒欽云：『二大老所謂一條拄杖兩人舁，被天寧拗作兩橛了也。』以拄杖倚左邊，云：『且聽各自平分。』」師云：「欽祖幸然拗折，今日不肖兒孫未免更將鸞膠為伊續起，逢人即出、逢人不出，兩彩一賽，如箭中的。金鳳銜華下彩樓，眼裏瞳人吹觱栗，三臺須是大家催，無限清風生八極。」白椎，云：「諦觀法王法，法王法如是。」卓拄杖一下，下座。勉參。「靈峰寺裏開爐，炭墼家常儘有，更賴現前兄弟，竭力同心出手。輕輕撥動火柴頭，烈燄亙天射牛斗，冷灰豆爆忽雷轟，叢林盡作師子吼。斷送生蛇化活龍，差排古佛離窠臼，無賓主句火爐頭，笑他趙老揚家醜。後來雪嵒欽又云：『不冷不熱爐鞴，半真半假金鋀，鑄作缾盤釵釧，卻成品字柴頭。』且道：與趙州無賓主話相去多少？若向者裏緇素得出，二大老性命在諸仁手裏；若緇素不出，諸仁性命卻在山僧手裏。」卓拄杖，云：「還委悉麼？莫向白雲深處坐，好看千嶂起風雷。」開爐，上堂。「烹佛烹祖大爐鞴，量等虛空包法界；煆凡煆聖惡鉗錘，千手大悲亦皺眉。鈍銕頑銅銷爍盡，精金美玉轉新奇，烈燄不

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 師林野奇老和尚，一任有鼻孔者，從教炙地薰天。」敷座，白椎竟，師云：「銕輪未轉，徹地轟天，略露風規，白雲萬里。還有寒毛卓豎者麼？出眾相見。」問：「芙蓉一向無人應，今日方知有主人，主人既至，請師作用。」師震威一喝，進云：「可謂正脈氣通欣此日，大悲松啟昔愁眉。」師云：「一彩兩賽。」進云：「銀蟾出海，誰不瞻光？」師云：「茅山土地。」問：「祖印高提，十方坐斷，入門一句，請師直指。」師云：「水深魚聚。」進云：「格外提持，萬人瞻仰，如何是芙蓉境？」師云：「入門一路大悲松。」進云：「當頭一句，截銕斬釘，如何是境中人？」師云：「獨坐孤峰遶萬峰。」進云：「人境已蒙師指示，向上一句又如何？」師云：「拄杖長七尺。」乃云：「銅峰疊翠，十里松陰，雲渡橋邊，龍吟虎嘯。來來亭畔，鳳翥麟翔，不問船來陸來，那管獅兒象兒？踏著祖翁田地，遂能丕振宗猷，始可起毓祖千年之舊案；大龐公三到之遺蹤，不須法堂探水、室內安盆，自然象鼻峰從茲通氣，大悲松得以揚眉，情與無情煥然等現，堪報不報之恩，共助無為之化。雖然，騰今耀古即不無，作麼生道箇玉轉珠回底句？會麼？一輪明月來峰頂，照徹支那百億洲。」復舉：「龐居士云：『十方同聚會』，金不博金；『箇箇學無為』，不從人得；『此是選佛場』，看腳下；『心空及第歸』，白雲萬里。」驀豎拄杖云：「龐居士在山僧拄杖頭上口喃喃道：『者廝兒切忌畫蛇添足。』」擲拄杖云：「識甚好惡？」下座。復位岳融領諸山，請上堂。「弘揚法化，銕蒺藜未許安閒；重建法幢，具眼者大家出手。起數年，鼓寂鐘沉之鄉；振今時，電掣雷轟之令。直得天花散彩、瓦礫生光、銅峰起舞、冷灶生煙。非假神通，全承渠力，不負初心，冀垂朗鑒。」下座。到船子，請上堂。問：「同源一會，不無上古風規；分座儼然，重整今時宗範。直入千峰即不問，腳踏雲間事若何？」師云：「霜風撲面寒。」進云：「芙蓉江上月，萬古照乾坤。」師云：「裂破腦門。」僧喝，師云：「著忙作麼？」進云：「也須勘過。」師云：「石人撫掌。」乃云：「罷釣龍淵逐野情，橫肩楖栗入深雲，此回為訪西林老，又出雲來到水濆。諸公還委悉麼？華亭孤月，千載遺風，門外剎竿，斬新條令。呈橈舞棹家聲異，釣盡江波得錦鱗。山僧雖然唱拍相隨，要且鼻孔各自出氣。今日到此，主賓互敬一句作麼生道？知心不在千盃酒，一盞清茶也醉人。」擊拂子，下

Senses.Explanation: Gratitude and shared benefit are joined in a compact formal saying. Feiyin and Yinyuan bring it into direct challenges, while Dabian and Zixian tie it to guiding others and sustaining a seat. Yuanan, Huiyue, and Yushan use it before turning to the next test their listeners must meet.

Senses.Explanation: The middle rung of the founding teacher's three-sentences ladder: waking in the second sentence makes one worthy to be a teacher for humans and gods. Linji Yixuan sets the ladder in his own seat, holding that his seeing is no different from the buddhas and ancestors, so that waking in the first sentence makes one their teacher, in the second a teacher for humans and gods, and in the third not even one's own savior, Shoushan Xingnian raises the ladder at the hall seat and answers each rung live, great use without lifting a brow and the staff that must draw blood, Tianyin Yuanxiu retells the ladder and its three couplets, then faults the master for adding a handle to the bowl with his nine-fold body talk that answers nothing of the truth, and Feiyin Tongrong quotes the ladder and reverses it at his Jing mountain seat, stone shoots sprouting, hemp returning beans, the lacquer bucket slow, laughing at the founder for forcing the sections, cutting water with a blade. Yinyuan Longqi wears the rung at the Buddha's birthday, telling the crowd that waking there makes one worthy to teach humans and gods and that a moment's doubt marks one a man who cannot save himself, then threading them through the founder's marrow, Jiqi Hongchu raises the family rule at the Hong mountain seat, asks whether the old man spoke truly, and rules otherwise, no place to talk, a load to carry out, and a soft weak plain truth, and Muchen Daomin lays the three sentences before the evening assembly, asking which rung they came out of, ready to vouch for the one who can say and to rule the one who cannot still without a seeker's eye, then taking it back for himself with the staff, a shout, and a walk to the quarters.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB189.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanyi Yu. While placing five people's bones in a tower, Sanyi Mingyu recalls companions of different surnames meeting as one family, then broken strings and a mournful night tune. Touching the five sets of bones with his staff, he says that even if they represented each of the five Chan houses he would bury them in one pit, leaving people with eyes horizontal and noses vertical. Mere pursuit of branches and leaves counts for little. Lifting the bones, he asks what fault these people have that warrants such language, then gives the general-and-peace pair. Sanyi owns both the ritual action and the appraisal; this is not a quoted ancient encounter. The named houses are not allowed to become a place in which to settle. The address does not identify the five deceased as the literal founders or report an actual military punishment.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB280.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yunwaize of Shending. Yunwai Xingze comments on Zhaozhou examining the old woman of Mount Tai. He says that she knows only how to urinate in bed with her eyes open, unaware that someone has exchanged her nose; Zhaozhou has accomplished a great deal, yet stands three feet deep in mud. Does anyone really see Zhaozhou? Yunwai gives the general-and-peace pair and an exclamation. The couplet is his present appraisal, not the old woman's directions or Zhaozhou's original reply. The first clause acknowledges hard-won success while the second prevents that success from becoming an unquestioned final verdict. Following verses take up roads, travelers describing their journey and peace established without warfare. They do not supply a literal account of the woman losing her nose or a rule that every examination succeeds.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB281.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zizhouchuan of Tanxi. Zizhou Chuan raises a monk asking Deshan what awakening is. Deshan strikes him and tells him to get out and stop fouling the place. Zizhou calls this grandmotherly kindness, says the monk lacks strength in his eyes, and adds that gold has its own price and is not sold mixed with sand. His verse first praises a commanding order transmitted through the ages and a general clearing disorder beyond the frontier, then gives the couplet. The headword is Zizhou's verse, distinct from Deshan's blow and reply. The acknowledgment of forceful efficacy turns immediately into exclusion from resting in its result. No response or final approval of the monk is recorded, and the military image does not establish a historical campaign behind the case.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB445.xml). Fellow-Disciples Record of Chan Master Bie’an. In Bie'an Xingtong's collection of fellow lineage members, a monk asks Wuyun about the claim that seeing one's nature makes one a Buddha: leaving becoming a Buddha aside, can the word 'seeing' itself still be admitted? Wuyun makes a retching sound. The subsequent master-comment gives the general-and-peace pair, followed by a verse saying a boat is unnecessary once ashore and arrival at the capital brings confidence of itself. The verse then sweeps away knowing, awareness, seeing and hearing. The pair belongs to the later appraisal, not the question or Wuyun's sound. It checks carrying the successful means or the claim to have seen forward as a possession after arrival. No further reply is supplied; the boat image is not a ban on ordinary perception.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB189.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanyi Yu. While placing five people's bones in a tower, Sanyi Mingyu recalls companions of different surnames meeting as one family, then broken strings and a mournful night tune. Touching the five sets of bones with his staff, he says that even if they represented each of the five Chan houses he would bury them in one pit, leaving people with eyes horizontal and noses vertical. Mere pursuit of branches and leaves counts for little. Lifting the bones, he asks what fault these people have that warrants such language, then gives the general-and-peace pair. Sanyi owns both the ritual action and the appraisal; this is not a quoted ancient encounter. The named houses are not allowed to become a place in which to settle. The address does not identify the five deceased as the literal founders or report an actual military punishment.

ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB280.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yunwaize of Shending. Yunwai Xingze comments on Zhaozhou examining the old woman of Mount Tai. He says that she knows only how to urinate in bed with her eyes open, unaware that someone has exchanged her nose; Zhaozhou has accomplished a great deal, yet stands three feet deep in mud. Does anyone really see Zhaozhou? Yunwai gives the general-and-peace pair and an exclamation. The couplet is his present appraisal, not the old woman's directions or Zhaozhou's original reply. The first clause acknowledges hard-won success while the second prevents that success from becoming an unquestioned final verdict. Following verses take up roads, travelers describing their journey and peace established without warfare. They do not supply a literal account of the woman losing her nose or a rule that every examination succeeds.

In Bie'an Xingtong's collection of fellow lineage members, a monk asks Wuyun about the claim that seeing one's nature makes one a Buddha: leaving becoming a Buddha aside, can the word 'seeing' itself still be admitted? Wuyun makes a retching sound. The subsequent master-comment gives the general-and-peace pair, followed by a verse saying a boat is unnecessary once ashore and arrival at the capital brings confidence of itself. The verse then sweeps away knowing, awareness, seeing and hearing. The pair belongs to the later appraisal, not the question or Wuyun's sound. It checks carrying the successful means or the claim to have seen forward as a possession after arrival. No further reply is supplied; the boat image is not a ban on ordinary perception.
ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 太平本是將軍定，不許將軍見太平

Senses.Explanation: The general establishes peace but is not allowed to enjoy or behold it. The reversal grants the efficacy of a decisive act while denying its agent a settled resting place in that success. Each application must be read with its own ritual or inherited encounter. While placing five people's bones in a tower, Sanyi Mingyu recalls companions of different surnames meeting as one family, then broken strings and a mournful night tune. Touching the five sets of bones with his staff, he says that even if they represented each of the five Chan houses he would bury them in one pit, leaving people with eyes horizontal and noses vertical. Mere pursuit of branches and leaves counts for little. Lifting the bones, he asks what fault these people have that warrants such language, then gives the general-and-peace pair. Sanyi owns both the ritual action and the appraisal; this is not a quoted ancient encounter. The named houses are not allowed to become a place in which to settle. The address does not identify the five deceased as the literal founders or report an actual military punishment. Yunwai Xingze comments on Zhaozhou examining the old woman of Mount Tai. He says that she knows only how to urinate in bed with her eyes open, unaware that someone has exchanged her nose; Zhaozhou has accomplished a great deal, yet stands three feet deep in mud. Does anyone really see Zhaozhou? Yunwai gives the general-and-peace pair and an exclamation. The couplet is his present appraisal, not the old woman's directions or Zhaozhou's original reply. The first clause acknowledges hard-won success while the second prevents that success from becoming an unquestioned final verdict. Following verses take up roads, travelers describing their journey and peace established without warfare. They do not supply a literal account of the woman losing her nose or a rule that every examination succeeds. Zizhou Chuan raises a monk asking Deshan what awakening is. Deshan strikes him and tells him to get out and stop fouling the place. Zizhou calls this grandmotherly kindness, says the monk lacks strength in his eyes, and adds that gold has its own price and is not sold mixed with sand. His verse first praises a commanding order transmitted through the ages and a general clearing disorder beyond the frontier, then gives the couplet. The headword is Zizhou's verse, distinct from Deshan's blow and reply. The acknowledgment of forceful efficacy turns immediately into exclusion from resting in its result. No response or final approval of the monk is recorded, and the military image does not establish a historical campaign behind the case. ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB305.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dayutao of Guoqing. He moves from literal victory to a warning against remaining in the conquering role.
ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 太平本是將軍致，不許將軍見太平

Senses.Explanation: The general brings about peace, but cannot claim to settle in it. Chan speakers use the military paradox to separate effective action from possession of its result. Feiyin turns the line on a hypothetical defender of his handling of old cases; Guxue caps a comparison of Panshan and Dahui with it. Hanyue applies it amid ordinary cycles of time; Dayu depicts discarded arms and village songs after victory, then refuses to let the victorious role remain.

Entries.SourceTerm: 太湖三萬六千頃，月在波心說向誰

Senses.PreferredTarget: Taihu stretches thirty-six thousand qing; to whom does the moon in its waves speak?
AlternateTargets: Across vast Taihu, to whom can the moon reflected in the water tell its story?
SearchAliases: Taihu moon in the waves to whom speak
moon on Taihu beyond verbal answer
Senses.Note: Taihu is pictured as vast, with the moon reflected at the center of its waves. The question asks who could receive a declaration from that scene. Zen teachers give the line as a response when an ordinary answer would narrow the point; it evokes a presence that is visible yet not delivered as an explanation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 設忌，上堂。「拄杖突出虛空，踢著通身粉碎。三炮四喝料揀，玄要賓主明歷。此是老和尚家醜，當陽露出端的。作麼是露出底句？咄！」明德居士請上堂。「踏破虛空口，崑崙顛倒走。明德出頭來，性哲傳燈久。」以拄杖畫相，云：「參！」聚雲三目法叔老和尚訃音至，上堂。「同住聚雲時，曾霑猶子愛，離亂各一方，面目無隔礙，化緣事已周，分身遍法界。大眾！還知者老漢落處麼？遇寒湖中向火，逢熱火裏乘涼，恁麼本分自由，好與頂門揭蓋。」復云：「蒼天！蒼天！」上堂。「扇子𨁝跳上三十三天，獅子窟中無異獸。觸著帝釋鼻孔，象王行處絕派蹤。東海鯉魚打一棒，萬里橫屍。雨似盆傾，四洲普潤。大眾！會麼？福城批判異諸方，大用全提只者是。」小參小參小參。「人天百萬，驀然拈花，此是瞿曇老漢上頭關；喚作竹篦則觸、不喚作竹篦則背，此是徑山老漢上頭關；一棒一條痕、一摑一掌血，此是慶忠老漢上頭關；逢人便拜、遇佛便打，此是福城長老上頭關。若在者裏一一會得，縱然一夜風吹去，只在蘆花淺水邊；如或未然，太湖三萬六千頃，月在波心說向誰？」小參。舉：「趙州和尚云：『老僧十二時中，除粥飯二時是雜用心處。』此是古人為敵生死底工夫，今人又當何如？若要擔荷佛祖門庭，須要箇直實決定志氣，千磨萬鍊，百棒打不回頭底漢子始得。若是半疑半信、半進半退底，終是半途而廢，安能在生死海中倒駕慈航耶？久立，眾慈各宜努力。」總戎袁寶善居士請小參。舉：「僧問趙州：『如何是祖師西來意？』州云：『庭前柏樹子。』僧云：『和尚莫將境示人。』州云：『我不將境示人。』僧云：『如何是祖師西來意？』州云：『庭前柏樹子。』者箇公案要累及寶善居士在。」示眾示眾午日，示眾。「石輥嚼破虛空，冤屈崑崙叫苦，痛殺海上王郎，到處敲鑼動鼓。」喝一喝，云：「家家蒲倚天寒，報到今朝是端午。」示眾。「生從何處來？死向何處去？知得來去處，方名學道人。」連喝四喝，云：「會得老僧者四喝，參學事畢。如或未然，但看受生死底是誰？不受生死底是誰？知得來去處底是誰？不知來去處底是誰？看來看去，看理會不得處，如一團火頓在胸中，久久提究到豁然貫通處，方知『生死』二字決定與自己不相干涉。」示眾。「今時學道人多是腳跟不穩、立志不堅，於世事上不如意，則火急要參禪、要修行；忽然世事稍有如意，則不參禪、不修行矣。此何以故？無決定信故也。如是學道，欲與

Senses.PreferredTarget: At the sun gate every day is triple autumn; before the moon hall every hour is nine summers
SearchAliases: at the sun gate every day is triple autumn; before the moon hall every hour is nine summers
Senses.Note: The old pair puts three autumns into each day at a sun gate and nine summers into each moment at a moon hall. Tian'an calls such talk odd and says cold is cold, heat is heat. Shaweng asks why snow fell last night if the sun gate works that way. Yuan'an uses the pair to join journey and home. When a monk asks Meixi about it, Meixi asks why anyone speaks of autumn and summer here. The whole pair tests fixed season and place, beyond the location phrase 'before the moon hall.'

Senses.Explanation: To cut off is to sever a flow, entanglement, division, or opening for continuation. An unnamed monk asks Guitong Huitong about the line that cuts off all streams. Yuanwu Keqin sings of cutting off all streams; Baiyu Jingsi and Dahui Zonggao speak of cutting through entanglements; Shoushan Xingnian says one word cuts off a thousand river mouths; Konggu Daocheng answers that sticks and shouts do not accommodate human feeling.

Senses.Note: “Cut off both ends” interrupts the choice a question has prepared. Wanru says it when asked whether to establish a particle; Yinyuan follows a blow with it in a travel question. Yichu says it while shutting off entry and exit at a retreat gate. Chaozong strikes in response to hiding and not hiding, while Baiyu asks what can be said if a middle is also disallowed. Lianyue gives the line as a present answer. None makes the phrase a third fixed side.

Senses.Explanation: To cut off the tongues of everyone under heaven is a hyperbolic appraisal for silencing every possible reply. Jiashan grants that the interlocutor can cut off everyone's tongue, then asks how a tongueless person could be made to speak. The bodily violence supplies the image, but the exchange tests the adequacy of a response rather than describing mutilation.

Senses.PreferredTarget: You may silence everyone's tongue; how will you make someone without a tongue speak?
SearchAliases: you may silence everyone's tongue; how will you make someone without a tongue speak?
Senses.Note: In Luopu's meeting with Jiashan, a shout does not finish the exchange. Jiashan grants that cutting off everyone's tongue is possible, then asks how to let a person with no tongue speak. Luopu falls silent and is struck. Sanshan treats the challenge as a decisive test; Hongzhi writes a verse about the tongueless person's expression. Liangting questions why Luopu could not move, Yikui asks how to answer, Tianran faults accepting Jiashan's words, and Gulin says Jiashan himself has not stopped everyone speaking. The line tests what remains after a forceful silencing.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X85/X85n1593.xml). Orthodox Line of the Chan School. Speaker: Deshan Yuanming. Deshan Yuanming presents cutting off every stream as one of three phrases shown to the assembly.

Senses.Explanation: In these records, 截斷眾流 names “cutting off every stream”: a saying or action that allows no further current, and the middle member of a recurring three-phrase set. Yuanwu Keqin uses the words for a solitary proclamation without turning back and explains the phrase beside encompassing heaven and earth and following the waves. Deshan Yuanming records the same three members explicitly. Unnamed monks ask Guizong Huitong, Shangfang Qiyue, Ruiyan Zhicai, and Rifang Shangzuo for the stream-cutting phrase; the recorded replies are an iron mountain across the road, a woman weeping at the Great Wall, “Good,” and a staff held crosswise. Tianyin Yuanxiu says that even cutting off every stream remains outside the gate, limiting any claim that the phrase itself marks final arrival.

Occurrences.Kwic: 方大聖人則名之曰咒，名之曰真言，如西方以水名蘇嚧巴，此生死心意識之見，而計名著相者也。以之為咒者，則曰唵蘇嚧莎訶。初無唵莎字為之函蓋，則墮生死見解。今以二字夾之，便成咒語。心意識不可到，而一切作用，靡不成就矣。前之問如何是西來意，言柏樹子。問如何是佛，言乾矢橛。雲門家有三句律之，以定宗旨。曰函蓋乾坤句，截斷眾流句，隨波逐浪句。以其函之蓋之，乾坤固密，便能截斷生死之流，不妨隨波不沉，逐浪不汩。今之一句咒語云唵折隸主隸準提莎訶，豈不函蓋乾坤。如此一句，豈不截斷生死。凡有所求也，則曰唵折隸主隸準提所求某事莎訶，豈非隨波逐浪之句乎。所以一大藏中，祕密之法頗多，而顯密圓通，則單示準提一法為則。若已悟者得之，則如龍得水，似虎

Senses.Explanation: The sentence that cuts off all streams: in Yunmen's three-sentence scheme, this is the word or move that stops the expected course of reply. Yuanwu Keqin says Yunmen's terse answer carries the covering, cutting-off, and wave-following functions together. Sanshan Denglai recounts how the old Yunmen saying was divided into these three named sentences. Hanyue Fazang lists the three as tests for how a phrase can work. Tianyin Yuanxiu sees all three functions in Yunmen's replies to a question about the moon in water. Xueyan Zuqin names the three categories and asks the assembly to recognize them in the present address. Feiyin Tongrong says he will probe the old three sentences further. Ruibai Mingxue calls his own shout a cutting-off sentence when it sweeps away distinctions between holy and ordinary and leaves no foothold for fixed understanding.

Senses.Explanation: To cut off the tangled vines is the records' recurring closure formula for ending the present chain of explanation, questioning, or verbal entanglement. Huanyou Chuan ends an account when tea arrives with 'cut off the tangled vines and drink tea.' Tianyin Xiu shouts the phrase after extended exhortation and, in another interview, draws once with his staff before saying it. Dahui Zonggao places it at the end of a written exposition whose paper has run out. Guxue Zhenzhe joins cutting the vines to overturning a nest of fixed formulations, while a later hall speaker makes the phrase itself the subject of a public question.

Senses.Explanation: To cut down a crane and lengthen a duck is to force naturally unequal creatures into an imposed measure. Chan masters use the paired action as an explicit appraisal of forced adjustment and contrast it with things proceeding of themselves. The cited passages span four works and preserve the exact headword in the quoted Chinese. The gloss reports the shared use and leaves each surrounding case to its own recorded exchange.

Senses.Explanation: The transmutation couplet — stir the long river into cream and turn the great earth to gold — asked whom it feeds at the Yuan hall seat, set past the slow waking, hung under the cicada's wing, refused as spendable coin, and filed under soul-playing from the Ming retreats to the Qing mountains. Chushi Fanqi, at the hall seat of the Benjue temple: stir the long river into cream and turn the great earth to gold — but to feed whom?; the whole ten directions are the monk's single eye — the walkers of water, land, and air, the winged and the wriggling — where do they light?; the buddhas are not my way — who then is the utmost of the way?; father and mother are not my kin — who then is the nearest kin?; Tianyin Yuanxiu, at the Qingshan seat in Jingxi, walks the assembly back from the sentence before sound — the scholars wear themselves out like apes grabbing at shadows — past the breaking of before-and-after, out beyond the far side of the primordial far shore, waking slowly back: to stir the long river into cream and turn the great earth to gold is nothing beyond one's share; but you must reach that field — and short of it, gouging the ancients' phrases — this is such-and-such a sentence, that is such-and-such — you may gouge down to Maitreya's next birth and it will only ever be just-so; Hanyue Fazang, at the Sheng'en temple on Dengwei mountain: the way weighs heavy through not-being and empties out through being; since it cannot be said and yet is said, every foot treads solid ground, every head is the native sky — thus it was said: the true person hides nothing in the mind and lets no word slip past the mouth, like a cicada wing sounding in the autumn wind, like a stiff wing perched on the empty sky — and so can stir the long river into cream and turn the great earth to gold; and what, then, is the way?; the shout, the long stillness, and: a spring pond brimming stored, an autumn wind fragrant in the grain. Tian'an Sheng, at the evening seat of the Great Awakening temple: stir the long river into cream and turn the great earth to gold — good at skimming the surplus to mend the want; but how does that compare with this Great Awakening, that clutches earth into gold every morning and will not spend one coin of it?; not stinginess, not spite — he wants his sons each to prop their own gate and pillar, spared being called the town's wastrel by the neighbors, broken and drifting, cursing father and reviling grandfather; and Baishan Dekai, instructing the assembly, files the whole apparatus under soul-playing: a blink of the eyes, soul-playing; sitting rapt in stillness, soul-playing; morning inquiry and evening greeting, soul-playing; even the whole storehouse of scriptures poured into the belly like water from a jar, soul-playing; the buddhas of the three times, the ancestors of the generations, every old abbot under heaven lifting the hammer and raising the whisk, soul-playing; and the seventeen hundred stale vines of the old cases, said longwise, said crosswise, said ten-ways-at-once — stir the long river into cream and turn the great earth to gold — soul-playing too; were one in the crowd to step out unbowed — Dragon-Mountain talks like this: has he no special power?; the mountain monk would tell him: no power at all — I only know hunger wants eating, fatigue wants sleeping, pain cries out, and itch laughs; and were someone to say that too is soul-playing — the monk can only laugh out loud; and what is the laugh about?; better to quarrel with the wise than to talk with the fool.

Senses.PreferredTarget: I am not convinced you have it yet
SearchAliases: i am not convinced you have it yet
Senses.Note: “I am not convinced you have it yet” is a refusal of easy certification. Linye says it after a monk’s polished flourish; Yushan after a monk claims to meet Nanquan face to face. Feiyin says it when a monk offers a poem about the road, and Yun’e after a smooth line on living with circumstances. Eryin says it after a monk declares that the whole has been laid open. Each teacher tests this response, not the student’s permanent capacity.

Senses.Explanation: The creed: not yet left Tusita, already in the royal palace; not yet out of the womb, the delivering of beings already done. The halls take it up on the buddha's birthday and on their own — and ask: who was delivered? Why then forty-nine years of talk, six years on the snow? Who received it: Tian'an Sheng is pressed straight — the delivering done before birth, who received it? — the donkey straightaway turns the mill; and before the gold cock crows? — daybreak and still dozing; Baiyu Jingsi is asked to rank it — the World-Honored finished before birth, and the master at the age of knowing fate has taught five assemblies: any better or worse? — a laugh at the edge of Jambudvipa; Lianfeng Su at the birth hall — the delivering done, the master stands here in person: what will he point with? — heaven covers without partiality, earth carries without partiality; Tianran Hanshi at the bath-buddha hall turns the creed inside out — was there really a Siddhartha in the Pure-rice king's palace? who then was teaching in Tusita? and how does one say not-yet-left-yet-already-descended? The slot it holds: Yikui Yuankui runs the school's sentences — crouching the tiger's head, gathering the tiger's tail, the first sentence makes the purport clear; not yet left Tusita, already descended to the royal palace, not yet out of the mother's womb, the delivering already done — the second; Shiyu Mingfang takes it to his own birthday hall — and after coming out of the womb? one great embarrassment — so that the stake-driving, oar-pulling, cable-holding, boat-loosing men of every generation all say it: without stepping he pervades the ten directions; Jifei Ruyi raises Nanquan, asked where the thus-come one would be born, drawing the circle on the table — grasp where that one circle lands and the delivering was done before birth, and crossing free of birth-and-death a mere idle thing; Liaozong Chaojian sets it under the eight-sided, unchanging pearl — since it is thus: say no, each endowed, each complete; say yes, and where is it right now?

Occurrences.Kwic: 成道業若為消，捫心幾箇知慚愧，今日三，明日四，閒處光陰盡虗棄，一朝老病來相尋，閻翁催請死符至，從前所作業不忘，三塗七趣從茲墜，袈裟失却復再難，鱗甲羽毛披則易，看他古之學道流，直忘人世輕名利，煑黃精，煨紫芋，飯一摶，水一器，為療形枯聊接氣，石爛松枯竟不知，洗心便作累生計，物外清閑一味高，世上黃金何足貴，劫空田地佛華開，香風觸破娘生鼻，選佛場中及第歸，圓覺伽藍恣遊戲，茲因結制夜小參，不覺所言成此偈。福源石屋珙禪師語錄卷之上福源石屋珙禪師語錄卷之下參學門人至柔等編山居詩山居詩余山林多暇，瞌睡之餘，偶成偈語自娛。紙墨少，便不欲紀之，雲衲禪人請書，蓋欲知我山中趣向。於是靜思，隨意走筆，不覺盈帙，故掩而歸之。復囑慎勿以此為歌詠之助，當須參意，則有激焉。吾家住在霅溪西，水滿天湖月滿溪。未到盡驚山險峻，曾來方識路高低。蝸涎素壁粘枯殻，虎過新蹄印雨泥。閒閉柴門春晝永，青桐花發𦘕胡啼。柴門雖設未甞關，閒看幽禽自往還，尺壁易求千丈石，黃金難買一生閒。雪消曉嶂聞寒瀑，葉落秋林見遠山，古栢煙消清晝永，是非不到白雲間。荒塚纍纍沒野蒿，昔人未葬盡金腰。有求莫若無求好，進步何如退步高。貪餌金鱗終落釜，出籠靈翮便冲霄。山翁不管紅塵事，自種青麻織布袍。紙窓竹屋槿籬笆，客到蒿湯便當茶，多見清貧長快樂，少聞濁富不驕奢。看經移案就明月，供佛簪瓶折野花，盡說上方兜率好，如何及得老僧家。道在人弘孰可憑，發言須與行相應。貪心似海何時足，妄念如苗逐日增。幾樹梅花清處士，一園芋子樂

Senses.Explanation: Before arriving, everyone fears the steep mountain; one who has been there knows the road rises and falls. Firsthand passage replaces imagined fear with knowledge of the actual path. Current deployments include Poshan Haiming in J26nB177, Jifei Ruyi in J38nB425, and Lüyan He in J39nB452. The full paired image remains the lexical unit. The line does not promise that the path is easy. Stonehouse introduces the Mountain Dwelling Poems as his own verses, then gives the paired line.

Senses.Explanation: “Not there yet” marks an answer, claim, or requested act as incomplete. Yangshan Huiji gives the verdict before adding a further response. Gulin Qingmao says it when attendants request a final verse and then writes one. Xuedou Chongxian rejects an earlier saying with the same words, Fushi Tongxian asks his attendant to say more, and Tianyin Yuanxiu refuses an attempted deception. In these passages the phrase postpones acceptance or completion in the immediate exchange.

Senses.Explanation: You have not even dreamed of it yet is a sharp Chan dismissal: speakers use it to reject a claimed understanding, display, comparison, or feat as not yet reaching the matter under discussion. Zhongfeng Mingben rejects elaborate identification of the 'person without rank' as not even its shadow. Yulin Tongxiu says that a dramatic exchange may manage shackles and locks while not yet dreaming of the teaching. Miyun Yuanwu applies the verdict to an elaborate explanation of Yunmen's cake. Wuhuan Xingchong gives it directly to a questioner who claims a view like snow on a red furnace, and Guting Shanjian applies it to Yantou's handling of the last word.

Occurrences.Kwic: 。「祖師關捩子，幽隱罕人知。」喝一喝，云：「開箇方便門，汝等從這裏入。」示眾。「馬祖道：『即心即佛。』南泉道：『不是心，不是佛，不是物。』國清放出赤肉團上無位真人，與汝大眾相見。」喝一喝，云：「未證據者看看。」示眾。「法身解說法，飽霜孤竹聲偏切；我說不得，帶火焦桐韻不悲。仰山推出枕子，溈山道：『用劍刃上事。』」連喝兩喝，云：「今日知音一任聽，師資心事不同時。」示眾。「瞿曇舌頭無骨，如是我聞；阿難皮下有血，信受奉行。」喝一喝，云：「國清敢道眼裏出火，可惜當時一千二百五十人中少箇男子。且道今日一眾又作麼生？」良久，云：「古之今之。」示眾。「千波競起，是文殊家風；一亙晴空，是普賢床榻。且道觀世音菩薩終日在什麼處？」良久，顧左右，云：「夜來風雨聲，花落知多少？」示眾。「萬法是心光，諸緣惟性曉，本無迷悟人，只要今日了。現前一眾盡是了事漢子，且道今日是什麼時節？」喝一喝，云：「不是不歸歸不得，五湖煙景有誰收？」示眾。「三世如來共一舌，鹹酸苦辣大家知；歷代祖師共一眼，青黃赤白同時見。秪如眼似枯井、舌如擂搥底，鹹酸苦辣辨不得、青黃赤白分不得，佛法靈騷在什麼處？」喝一喝，云：「誌公不是閑和尚。」示眾。「未明心地印，難透祖師關；欲透祖師關，須明心地印。」拈起拄杖，云：「這箇是心地印。」畫一畫，云：「這箇是祖師關。已過關者，掉臂竟去；未過關者，且借印看。」良久，喝一喝，云：「莫怪適來頻勘驗，自從別後見君希。」示眾。「拓開無上玅門，青山依舊青；揭示第一義諦，白雲依舊白。德山棒，好肉剜瘡；臨濟喝，虛空著楔。三世諸佛不知有，黎奴白牯卻知有，道人行處如火消冰，動靜去來該他不著，甚處討他三玄五位、六相九帶？」顧左右，云：「且道國清為人在甚麼處？」良久，云：「莫妄想。」示眾。「有一句到你，釋迦自釋迦；無一句到你，彌勒自彌勒；有無俱不到，然燈與你授記，當來必定成佛。且道：居何國土？作麼度人？」喝一喝，云：「路逢死蛇莫打殺，沒底籃子盛將歸。」示眾。「三四五六七八九，石人伸出兩隻手。普賢白象睡正濃，文殊青獅夢作狗。觀音菩薩嘗惺惺，怪他彌勒不唧溜。明州市裏等箇人，直至而今兩頭走。國清與箇方便。」喝一喝，云：「一葉落，天下秋。」示眾。「明日有人請說法，夜來先自苦愁煞。思量無計可安排，不如且念摩訶薩。唐言正覺，梵語菩薩。我是老實人，不會多忉怛。」喝一喝，「祥麟只有一隻角。」示眾。「拈華端的意，一笑豈徒然？倒卻剎竿後，依然年復年。臨濟

Occurrences.Kwic: 也，諸人向甚麼處安身立命？若者裏著得隻眼，三世諸佛在火燄上轉大法輪；其或未然，火燄燒殺三世諸佛。」上堂。問：「向上宗乘即不問，開爐一句是如何？」師云：「河無聲，狐始渡。」進云：「學人則不然。」師云：「你試亂統看。」進云：「大家團圞頭，共說無生話。」師云：「如何是無生話？」僧一喝，師云：「胡喝亂喝。」問：「人人本具，箇箇不無，大覺開爐，又煆煉箇甚麼？」師云：「一言既出，駟馬難追。」進云：「恁麼則蹋破艸鞋無覓處，得來全不費工夫。」師云：「如何是你不費工夫底句子？」進云：「大家抖擻精神去，親到靈山大徹堂。」師云：「太費力生。」進云：「謝師畣話。」師云：「好惡不識。」問：「今朝結制，端為何事？」師云：「馬頭覓角。」乃云：「今朝大覺開爐，奉告龍神土地：一、要叢林無難無災，二、要禪流少病少惱，三、要二時粥足飯足，四、要執事大小和諧。更有一要，山僧不能說得。何故？一字入公門，九牛拔不出。」晚參。「佩羅山劍，張石鞏弓，跨西河師子，射長沙大蟲，寶岸盡蹋倒，狐兔死無蹤。有意氣，添豪雄，年來老大疏慵甚，順朱村院教蒙童。蒙童蒙童，莫辱祖翁，子不我搆，我心忡忡。我之悠懷，熱炙於衷，惟子憫念，及第心空。」晚參。「未明心地印，難透祖師關。作麼生是心地印？初三初四月如鉤。」晚參。「金毛師子喋屎狗，白象王兒推磨驢，應如是知、如是見、如是信解，不生法相，直饒恁麼，未免陳老師簡點在。」上堂。問：「刮去髓，存箇甚麼？」師云：「描也描不成，畫也畫不就。」進云：「雖然不離人間世，別是人間一洞天。」師云：「那裏是別洞天？」進云：「大家在者裏。」師云：「學語之流，一札千行。」問：「眾色歸空，空歸何所？」師云：「寒風劈面急。」乃拈拄杖，云：「有利、無利，不離行市，我今為汝保任此事，終不虛也。」擿下，云：「不得春風華不開，及至華開又吹落。」冬夜，小參。「朔風凜凜，寒月絲絲，書雲節屆，大地咸知，畢竟陽來何所？試看陰去何之。好消息，露風規，何事男兒眼搭眵？」上堂。問：「天寒地寒、冰霜凜冽；佛寒祖寒，鼻孔貫穿。應時一句，便請師宣。」師云：「問得卻好。」進云：「還許學人請益也未？」師云：「祇許一，不許二。」進云：「拈卻一二義，否極泰方來。」師云：「客情步步隨人轉。」進云：「莫便是指蹤學人處麼？」師云：「山僧忍笑不禁。」問：「陽極陰生、陰極陽生，只如陰陽不到處是何消息？」師云：「文殊堂裏萬菩薩。」進云：「恁麼則塵中能作主，化外自來賓。」師云：「古人

Occurrences.Kwic: 未知向上一竅。所以道，此事如擊石火、似閃電光，搆得搆不得，未免喪身失命。到箇裏、撥一線道、拶透全機，便可坐斷毘盧頂、不稟釋迦文，說什麼露柱著衫南嶽去、燈籠脫帽上天台，一任天上人間逍遙自在；其或未然，饒伊走盡天涯，大有人穿卻鼻孔。」喝一喝，卓拄杖。雲居大眾設齋請上堂：「擊碎驪龍明月珠，縱橫無住；跳出無生獅子窟，哮吼驚群。透頂透底絕羅籠，亙古亙今無背向。山僧昔住雲居，如羚羊挂角杳絕蹤繇，今者來茲石霜，合水和泥，通身露布。與麼中不與麼，暗透兩重關；不與麼中卻與麼，全提向上路。敢問大眾，且道住雲居、住石霜，畢竟是一是二？豈容淺見衲僧會，唯許通方作者知。」喝一喝。往浙歸上堂，舉：「黃龍南禪師出山歸，有頌云：『去時一溪流水送，回來滿谷白雲迎，一身去住非去住，二物無情似有情應。』菴老祖出山歸，亦有頌云：『去時冒雨連宵去，回來帶水復拖泥，自怪一生無定力，尋常多被業風吹。』」師云：「二大老美則美矣，未免太波挈生。山僧亦有一頌舉似大眾：去日煙波萬里遙，回時風月杖頭挑，乾坤老我無拘束，閒殺龍門萬仞標。」結制上堂：大無外、小無內，拋擲百千三昧；句亦鏟、意亦鏟，閃爍摩醯隻眼，坐斷千聖頂𩕳，一一珠回玉轉。所以道，未明心地印，難透祖師關，透過祖師關，全彰心地印。臨濟喫黃檗六十痛棒，高安灘上知歸；興化被大覺脫下衲衣，親見臨濟在黃檗喫棒底道理。如斯標格，脫體現前，一句當天，迥絕依倚。到箇裏，何修不證、何覺不圓？出沒卷舒，頭正尾正，且不涉功勳直下坐斷一句作麼生道？蒲團靜倚無餘事，永日寥寥賀太平。」復舉：「黃龍南禪師云：『世間有五種不易：第一施者不易；第二化者不易；第三轉生作熟不易；第四端坐食者不易；且道第五不易是甚麼人？』良久云：『聻。』下座。時翠嵒真為首座，藏主問真：『第五不易是誰？』真云：『腦後見腮，莫與往來。』石霜即不然，第五不易是誰？有眼無耳朵，六月火邊坐。」晚參：「萬法是心光，諸緣惟性曉，本無迷悟人，只要今日了。」驀拈拄杖云：「拄杖子穿卻諸人鼻孔即不問，秖如昨日晴、今日雨，畢竟明甚麼邊事？」喝一喝云：「在家疑是客，別國卻為親。」解制上堂：四月十五日結，七月十五日解，明月珠旋冰玉盤，千眼大悲鬥光彩。喝。中秋上堂：見山不是山，見水何魯別，山河及大地，都是一輪月。大眾！古德恁麼道，一時漏逗了也。山河大地既是一輪月，則無古今圓缺之殊，寧有去來明暗之相？十虛通徹高下混融，乾轉坤旋攝他不著，說什麼描不成畫不就，昨夜三更白如晝

Occurrences.Kwic: 眾代語，眾競下語，師俱不肯，乃代云：「但以假名字，引導於眾生。」問眾：「是處是慈氏，無門無善財。因甚道琉璃殿上無知識？」眾下語不契，師代云：「江南地暖，塞北天寒。」問眾：「有人犯罪當處決，若殺則違佛戒，不殺又違王令，且作麼生處斷？」眾下語不契，師代云：「格。」問眾：「六箇骰子滿盆紅，作麼生賽？」眾下語不契，師代云：「好手不彰名。」有誦經僧喫齋次，居士問：「經中道：『無眼、耳、鼻、舌、身、意』，將甚麼喫齋？」僧無對。士舉似師，求代語，師云：「孟八郎漢又恁麼去也。」眾諷經次，師問云：「白底是紙，黑底是字，那箇是汝等諷底經？」定云：「鐘鼓分明。」系云：「向下文長，明日與和尚道。」明一云：「滿口道不出。」密堅云：「諦聽，諦聽。」師俱不肯，乃云：「穿雲俊鶻，便合乘時；止濼困魚，徒勞激浪。」紹云：「求波不離水。」師云：「切忌沒頭浸殺。」問眾：「不萌之艸如何藏得香象？」眾競下語，師俱不肯，乃代云：「海闊山高。」問眾：「教中道：『知有涅槃，不戀三界。』意旨如何？」眾下語不契，師代云：「似將黃葉止兒啼。」問眾：「重陽九日菊花新，意旨如何？」眾下語不契，師代云：「知音不用頻頻舉，達者應須暗裏驚。」問眾：「未明心地印，難透祖師關。如何是心地印？」系云：「片月澄空。」師云：「也只道得一半。」系云：「和尚作麼生？」師云：「屋破見青天。」一日，舉：「古德云：『一念不落諸緣，證取自家境界。』」師云：「大小古德慣捏死蛇頭，未解變通在。山僧不然，假饒念念攀緣，不離自家境界。」復顧眾云：「如何是自家境界？」昂云：「癢處多搔。」師云：「放汝三十棒。」眾競下語，師俱不肯，乃代云：「逆則嗔，順則喜。」問眾：「盡大地是吹毛利劍，你向甚麼處存扎？」紹云：「金不博金。」師云：「學語之流。」紹云：「是何言歟？」師云：「盡大地是火坑，得何三昧不被燒卻？」紹云：「箇中無別物。」師云：「者是茶鍾，者是茶壺，作麼生說箇無別物底道理？」紹云：「和尚莫眼花。」師云：「放汝三十棒。」問眾：「既是透網金鱗，因甚麼重重點額？」緒云：「卻是和尚鈍置某甲。」師云：「且莫錯怪山僧。」眾下語不契，師代云：「何不道：『伯牙縱有高山調，不遇知音也是閑』？」問眾：「不見一法是你諸人眼睛，者是蒲團，者是香版，作麼生說箇不見一法底道理？」紹云：「天上天下，唯我獨尊。」師云：「爭奈蒲團、香版何？」紹云：「和尚莫錯認。」師云：「如何是不錯認？」紹云：「天上天下，唯我獨尊。」師

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 也，諸人向甚麼處安身立命？若者裏著得隻眼，三世諸佛在火燄上轉大法輪；其或未然，火燄燒殺三世諸佛。」上堂。問：「向上宗乘即不問，開爐一句是如何？」師云：「河無聲，狐始渡。」進云：「學人則不然。」師云：「你試亂統看。」進云：「大家團圞頭，共說無生話。」師云：「如何是無生話？」僧一喝，師云：「胡喝亂喝。」問：「人人本具，箇箇不無，大覺開爐，又煆煉箇甚麼？」師云：「一言既出，駟馬難追。」進云：「恁麼則蹋破艸鞋無覓處，得來全不費工夫。」師云：「如何是你不費工夫底句子？」進云：「大家抖擻精神去，親到靈山大徹堂。」師云：「太費力生。」進云：「謝師畣話。」師云：「好惡不識。」問：「今朝結制，端為何事？」師云：「馬頭覓角。」乃云：「今朝大覺開爐，奉告龍神土地：一、要叢林無難無災，二、要禪流少病少惱，三、要二時粥足飯足，四、要執事大小和諧。更有一要，山僧不能說得。何故？一字入公門，九牛拔不出。」晚參。「佩羅山劍，張石鞏弓，跨西河師子，射長沙大蟲，寶岸盡蹋倒，狐兔死無蹤。有意氣，添豪雄，年來老大疏慵甚，順朱村院教蒙童。蒙童蒙童，莫辱祖翁，子不我搆，我心忡忡。我之悠懷，熱炙於衷，惟子憫念，及第心空。」晚參。「未明心地印，難透祖師關。作麼生是心地印？初三初四月如鉤。」晚參。「金毛師子喋屎狗，白象王兒推磨驢，應如是知、如是見、如是信解，不生法相，直饒恁麼，未免陳老師簡點在。」上堂。問：「刮去髓，存箇甚麼？」師云：「描也描不成，畫也畫不就。」進云：「雖然不離人間世，別是人間一洞天。」師云：「那裏是別洞天？」進云：「大家在者裏。」師云：「學語之流，一札千行。」問：「眾色歸空，空歸何所？」師云：「寒風劈面急。」乃拈拄杖，云：「有利、無利，不離行市，我今為汝保任此事，終不虛也。」擿下，云：「不得春風華不開，及至華開又吹落。」冬夜，小參。「朔風凜凜，寒月絲絲，書雲節屆，大地咸知，畢竟陽來何所？試看陰去何之。好消息，露風規，何事男兒眼搭眵？」上堂。問：「天寒地寒、冰霜凜冽；佛寒祖寒，鼻孔貫穿。應時一句，便請師宣。」師云：「問得卻好。」進云：「還許學人請益也未？」師云：「祇許一，不許二。」進云：「拈卻一二義，否極泰方來。」師云：「客情步步隨人轉。」進云：「莫便是指蹤學人處麼？」師云：「山僧忍笑不禁。」問：「陽極陰生、陰極陽生，只如陰陽不到處是何消息？」師云：「文殊堂裏萬菩薩。」進云：「恁麼則塵中能作主，化外自來賓。」師云：「古人

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 未知向上一竅。所以道，此事如擊石火、似閃電光，搆得搆不得，未免喪身失命。到箇裏、撥一線道、拶透全機，便可坐斷毘盧頂、不稟釋迦文，說什麼露柱著衫南嶽去、燈籠脫帽上天台，一任天上人間逍遙自在；其或未然，饒伊走盡天涯，大有人穿卻鼻孔。」喝一喝，卓拄杖。雲居大眾設齋請上堂：「擊碎驪龍明月珠，縱橫無住；跳出無生獅子窟，哮吼驚群。透頂透底絕羅籠，亙古亙今無背向。山僧昔住雲居，如羚羊挂角杳絕蹤繇，今者來茲石霜，合水和泥，通身露布。與麼中不與麼，暗透兩重關；不與麼中卻與麼，全提向上路。敢問大眾，且道住雲居、住石霜，畢竟是一是二？豈容淺見衲僧會，唯許通方作者知。」喝一喝。往浙歸上堂，舉：「黃龍南禪師出山歸，有頌云：『去時一溪流水送，回來滿谷白雲迎，一身去住非去住，二物無情似有情應。』菴老祖出山歸，亦有頌云：『去時冒雨連宵去，回來帶水復拖泥，自怪一生無定力，尋常多被業風吹。』」師云：「二大老美則美矣，未免太波挈生。山僧亦有一頌舉似大眾：去日煙波萬里遙，回時風月杖頭挑，乾坤老我無拘束，閒殺龍門萬仞標。」結制上堂：大無外、小無內，拋擲百千三昧；句亦鏟、意亦鏟，閃爍摩醯隻眼，坐斷千聖頂𩕳，一一珠回玉轉。所以道，未明心地印，難透祖師關，透過祖師關，全彰心地印。臨濟喫黃檗六十痛棒，高安灘上知歸；興化被大覺脫下衲衣，親見臨濟在黃檗喫棒底道理。如斯標格，脫體現前，一句當天，迥絕依倚。到箇裏，何修不證、何覺不圓？出沒卷舒，頭正尾正，且不涉功勳直下坐斷一句作麼生道？蒲團靜倚無餘事，永日寥寥賀太平。」復舉：「黃龍南禪師云：『世間有五種不易：第一施者不易；第二化者不易；第三轉生作熟不易；第四端坐食者不易；且道第五不易是甚麼人？』良久云：『聻。』下座。時翠嵒真為首座，藏主問真：『第五不易是誰？』真云：『腦後見腮，莫與往來。』石霜即不然，第五不易是誰？有眼無耳朵，六月火邊坐。」晚參：「萬法是心光，諸緣惟性曉，本無迷悟人，只要今日了。」驀拈拄杖云：「拄杖子穿卻諸人鼻孔即不問，秖如昨日晴、今日雨，畢竟明甚麼邊事？」喝一喝云：「在家疑是客，別國卻為親。」解制上堂：四月十五日結，七月十五日解，明月珠旋冰玉盤，千眼大悲鬥光彩。喝。中秋上堂：見山不是山，見水何魯別，山河及大地，都是一輪月。大眾！古德恁麼道，一時漏逗了也。山河大地既是一輪月，則無古今圓缺之殊，寧有去來明暗之相？十虛通徹高下混融，乾轉坤旋攝他不著，說什麼描不成畫不就，昨夜三更白如晝

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 眾代語，眾競下語，師俱不肯，乃代云：「但以假名字，引導於眾生。」問眾：「是處是慈氏，無門無善財。因甚道琉璃殿上無知識？」眾下語不契，師代云：「江南地暖，塞北天寒。」問眾：「有人犯罪當處決，若殺則違佛戒，不殺又違王令，且作麼生處斷？」眾下語不契，師代云：「格。」問眾：「六箇骰子滿盆紅，作麼生賽？」眾下語不契，師代云：「好手不彰名。」有誦經僧喫齋次，居士問：「經中道：『無眼、耳、鼻、舌、身、意』，將甚麼喫齋？」僧無對。士舉似師，求代語，師云：「孟八郎漢又恁麼去也。」眾諷經次，師問云：「白底是紙，黑底是字，那箇是汝等諷底經？」定云：「鐘鼓分明。」系云：「向下文長，明日與和尚道。」明一云：「滿口道不出。」密堅云：「諦聽，諦聽。」師俱不肯，乃云：「穿雲俊鶻，便合乘時；止濼困魚，徒勞激浪。」紹云：「求波不離水。」師云：「切忌沒頭浸殺。」問眾：「不萌之艸如何藏得香象？」眾競下語，師俱不肯，乃代云：「海闊山高。」問眾：「教中道：『知有涅槃，不戀三界。』意旨如何？」眾下語不契，師代云：「似將黃葉止兒啼。」問眾：「重陽九日菊花新，意旨如何？」眾下語不契，師代云：「知音不用頻頻舉，達者應須暗裏驚。」問眾：「未明心地印，難透祖師關。如何是心地印？」系云：「片月澄空。」師云：「也只道得一半。」系云：「和尚作麼生？」師云：「屋破見青天。」一日，舉：「古德云：『一念不落諸緣，證取自家境界。』」師云：「大小古德慣捏死蛇頭，未解變通在。山僧不然，假饒念念攀緣，不離自家境界。」復顧眾云：「如何是自家境界？」昂云：「癢處多搔。」師云：「放汝三十棒。」眾競下語，師俱不肯，乃代云：「逆則嗔，順則喜。」問眾：「盡大地是吹毛利劍，你向甚麼處存扎？」紹云：「金不博金。」師云：「學語之流。」紹云：「是何言歟？」師云：「盡大地是火坑，得何三昧不被燒卻？」紹云：「箇中無別物。」師云：「者是茶鍾，者是茶壺，作麼生說箇無別物底道理？」紹云：「和尚莫眼花。」師云：「放汝三十棒。」問眾：「既是透網金鱗，因甚麼重重點額？」緒云：「卻是和尚鈍置某甲。」師云：「且莫錯怪山僧。」眾下語不契，師代云：「何不道：『伯牙縱有高山調，不遇知音也是閑』？」問眾：「不見一法是你諸人眼睛，者是蒲團，者是香版，作麼生說箇不見一法底道理？」紹云：「天上天下，唯我獨尊。」師云：「爭奈蒲團、香版何？」紹云：「和尚莫錯認。」師云：「如何是不錯認？」紹云：「天上天下，唯我獨尊。」師

Senses.Explanation: Without understanding the seal of the mind ground, it is hard to pass the ancestors' barrier. The pair links passing the ancestral barrier to direct understanding of mind. Current sources: Dayu Tao in J34nB305, Tian'an Sheng in J26nB187, Erzhan Zun in J27nB200, Lu'yan He in J39nB452. The complete saying and source turn control the sense. It is a practical challenge, not an administrative credential.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問如何是佛。師曰。如何不是佛。問未曉。玄言。請師直指。師曰。家住海門洲。扶桑最先照。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T51/T51n2076.xml). Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp. An unnamed monk asks Fengxue Yanzhao what Buddha is. Fengxue replies by asking how anything is not Buddha. The monk says he has not understood these profound words and asks the teacher to point directly. Fengxue answers that his home is in Haimen, where Fusang receives the first light. The headword is the monk's follow-up request, explicitly prompted by failure to understand the preceding reply; the geographical and dawn image is Fengxue's answer. The passage does not name the monk or explain that image as a doctrine or a literal location where Buddha is to be found. Its promise of directness remains something to examine in the actual reply, rather than a guarantee of an abstract explanation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：「古人答話，劈腹開心，頗奈師僧未得性燥。即今若有問昭覺：『如何是佛？』答伊：『何更覓佛？』又云：『未曉玄言，請師直指。』答云：『門前駟馬橋，松杉四圍繞。』委悉麼？長笛一聲牽海浪，江風山月盡皆聞。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB371.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Foyuan. Foyuan Chegang first raises Fengxue's exchange, saying the ancients answered with their bellies split and hearts open, although the monk had not yet become sufficiently urgent. He then explicitly proposes what would happen if someone asked him at Zhaojue what Buddha is: why seek Buddha again? If the proposed questioner repeated the request for a direct indication, Foyuan would answer with Sima Bridge before the gate, surrounded by pines and firs. Do they understand? He closes with one long flute note drawing the sea's waves, heard throughout river wind and mountain moonlight. The retained headword belongs to this hypothetical requester, not to Foyuan asking his own teacher and not to an identified second historical monk. Foyuan's new local answer makes a present teaching use of the old conversational form while leaving its imagery open.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Before any world existed, this nature was already here
AlternateTargets: Before there was a world, this nature was present already
Senses.Note: “Before any world existed, this nature was already here” is paired in the sources with the claim that this nature does not perish when a world does. Zhaozhou voices it while warning listeners against searching outside themselves. Shitian asks a student what this nature is; Duanqiao and Defeng reconsider the old exchange in which Zhaozhou points to the four elements and five aggregates. Wu’an uses the line to speak of the teaching before Buddhas appear. The point is tested through present experience.

Occurrences.Kwic: 印，可據師繩為二祖。繼得三祖，乃是白衣居士，儒釋之教，無不精通。忽患風恙，特來問法於二祖云：弟子身纏風恙，乞師懺罪。二祖更不移易一絲毫子，便云：將罪來，與汝懺。三祖亦如是，推窮無計，乃云：內外覓罪，了不可得。二祖仍將所得底印子一塔，云：與汝懺罪竟。佛佛授手，祖祖相傳，直至今日。所以靈山拈花一節，謂之教外別行。既是經律論皆包括在中，更不單單具載。是知我此宗門，猶如大海，百川異流，莫不同歸一味。如太虗空，盡百億恒河沙世界，無不包容。所以道：未有世界，早有此性。世界壞時，此性不壞。諸佛未出世，祖師未西來，人人常光現前，箇箇壁立千仞。在聖不增一絲毫，在凡不減一絲毫。惟是迷悟有殊，所以聖凡有異。遂致執泥文字之學滋多，本有之性不能發現。背覺合塵，弃本逐末，葢由是矣。儒教亦云：君子務本，本立而道生。此本即是自己本命元辰，本來面目。得此本立，方可得道生。本若不立，何緣得道生？此是儒家膚淺之教，尚且說得如此親切，何況不傳之妙者耶。是汝諸人，若要真箇參禪學道，究明生死大事，以徹證為期者，第一須具堅久身心。

Senses.Explanation: “Before any world existed, this nature was already here” is a claim teachers immediately put to the test. Zhaozhou voices the line and Shitian asks what this nature means for a student now. Duanqiao and Defeng challenge an old question about it; Wu’an uses it to speak of teaching before Buddhas.

Entries.SourceTerm: 未有常行而不住，未有常住而不行

Senses.PreferredTarget: There is no continual going without staying, and no continual staying without going
AlternateTargets: One cannot keep going without staying, nor keep staying without going
SearchAliases: constant going not without staying constant staying not without going
Senses.Note: Mazu gives the saying to Yaoshan while sending him to teach elsewhere. Its paired clauses make going and staying mutually implicated rather than fixed alternatives. Later masters use it when addressing travel, residence, and whether a person can act freely in either condition.

Senses.Explanation: Going and staying are presented as mutually implicated, not separate fixed positions. Mazu says the paired line to Yaoshan, then urges him to serve as a ferry for others rather than remain where he is. Sanyi uses it after invoking the Buddha-place contrast; Fangrong says it at the end of a retreat and asks where going and staying belong. Yingning applies it to movement without a fixed abode; Azi invokes it after crossing a mountain pass and tests both directions.

Entries.SourceTerm: 未有長行而不住，未有長住而不行

Senses.PreferredTarget: No one travels forever without stopping; no one stays forever without moving.
AlternateTargets: There is no perpetual going without dwelling, nor perpetual dwelling without going.
Senses.Note: The local challenge and the current teacher's response govern the reading; quoted evaluations are not universal factual claims.

Occurrences.Kwic: 祖曰：不然，未有長行而不住，未有長住而不行，欲益而無所益，欲為而無所為，宜作舟航，莫久住此。山於是禮辭，再返石頭。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X67/X67n1309.xml). Treasury of the True Dharma Eye. The inherited Yaoshan case says Mazu praises Yaoshan's realization and tells him to bind his belly with three strips and establish himself on a mountain. Yaoshan asks who he is to dare do so. Mazu replies that no one keeps traveling without staying or stays forever without traveling, then urges him to become a ferry for others and not remain here long. Dahui later comments on the connected Yaoshan and Shitou episode, praising its genuine exchange. The headword belongs to Mazu's quoted encouragement: staying and movement are both part of helping others, rather than evidence that the teacher's student must remain dependent on him indefinitely.

Occurrences.Kwic: 戊午臘月十八日退院上堂師舉：「古云：『未有長行而不住，未有長住而不行。』所以道：人去住如行雲流水，了無滯礙。山僧曩承闔郡護法、諸山耆宿，及本寺經主、十地諸師命主楞嚴法席，自慚未具磨磚之手，兼乏匡眾之才，無補叢林，虛消信施，有負緇素大德！今日人天眾前舉揚箇事，願諸檀護及眾師友公請高德之士以繼此席，大轉法輪，方不負紫柏尊者、密藏大師之宏願也。既然如是，秪如即今退院一句作麼生道？」驀豎拄杖，云：「今朝楖栗化龍去，仍藉飛騰六合雲。」以拄杖橫肩，下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB221.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Faxiyin on the Śūraṅgama. On leaving his abbacy, Faxi Yin raises the ancient traveling-and-staying pair and says going or remaining should resemble flowing clouds and water without obstruction. He recalls accepting the teaching seat at the request of patrons and elders, criticizes his own inability to benefit the monastery and asks them to invite a worthier successor. What sentence expresses his departure now? Raising his staff, he says it becomes a dragon taking flight with the clouds, places it across his shoulder and descends. The headword is the inherited Mazu saying, while the public resignation and gesture supply its present application; the self-criticism need not be read as an independently proved failure.

Occurrences.Kwic: 復田別駕素庵復田別駕素庵古德云：未有長行而不住，未有長住而不行。縱揮麈談心，固是垂手機關，然遺藥他方，亦未是懶惰偷閒也。三接追札，更見為法之誠、慕道之切。所可憚者，錦衣未披，銅章未握，詎肯效西堂懶公耶？幸臨濟之後，有願過李楊之門者，堯舜與人同耳。居士大有餘裕哉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB239.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chuiwan. In a letter replying to Tian, Juyun Chuiwan Guangzhen cites the old saying about neither traveling nor staying perpetually. Speaking together is one way to offer help, he says, but leaving medicine elsewhere is not laziness or stolen leisure either. Tian's repeated letters show earnestness for the teaching, and the reply considers official responsibilities and another meeting. The headword remains Mazu's inherited formulation rather than a newly reported autobiographical saying by the letter writer. It lets the correspondent's wish to retain the teacher be acknowledged while defending help given through departure and correspondence as well as continued physical presence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 新命移忠西源長老，久居板首，表率人天，已具向上爪牙、作家手段。茲以時節既至，大丞相符命自來，驩動叢林，聲播海內。古德道：未有長行而不住，未有長住而不行。欲益無所益，欲為無所為。宜作舟航，廣度群品。雖然，且山僧末後一句如何舉似？莫負王臣外護恩，好與佛祖作頭抵。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1410.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tanfang Shouzhong. When the senior monk Xiyuan Da takes an abbacy at Yizhong, Tanfang Shouzhong recalls successive ancestral transmissions, including Linji leaving Huangbo with vigorous reciprocal blows. He praises the appointee's developed ability and quotes the ancient traveling-and-staying pair with its continuation: act without a fixed object of benefit, become a ferry and carry beings across. His final instruction is not to betray the external support of ruler and ministers and to stand up for the Buddha and ancestors. The exact headword is the inherited Mazu saying; the present occasion uses it to authorize the monk's departure into public responsibility, not mere wandering for personal preference.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：一向面壁，道絕人荒；一向貪程，眼瞤耳熱。未有長行而不住，未有長住而不行。或時十字街頭拈起拄杖，和其光、同其塵，灼然一切處光明燦爛去；或時孤峯頂上放下鉢囊，杜其谿、塞其穴，灼然一切處枯淡去。即心是佛也不得，非心非佛也不得，不是心、不是佛、不是物也不得。我見兩箇泥牛鬬入海，直至如今無消息。喝一喝。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1420.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi. Chushi Fanqi first warns that perpetual wall-facing leaves the way deserted, while constant pursuit of a journey makes eyes and ears strained. He revoices the pair about neither moving nor remaining forever, then gives two modes: raise the staff in the crowded street, sharing its light and dust, or put down the bowl on a solitary peak in plain austerity. Neither 'mind is Buddha' nor its familiar negations will settle it. His cap has two clay oxen disappear into the sea, followed by a shout. The headword is his present synthesis of inherited language, resisting exclusive commitment to either seclusion or public activity rather than laying out a compulsory timetable for alternating them.

Senses.Explanation: Before one’s parents were born marks the side of the encounter before social identity and discriminating categories are asserted. Masters demand that hearers look there, then test attachment even to that position. A temporal phrase becomes a live question about the respondent before inherited names and divisions, not speculation about prenatal chronology. The records also warn that resting there can already be mud underfoot; the entry therefore does not make the phrase a final answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 浮山遠錄公云。未透底人參句不如參意。透得底人。參意不如參句。雲門下有三尊宿。答吹毛劍俱云了。唯是巴陵答得過於了字。此乃得句也。且道。了字與珊瑚枝枝撐著月。是同是別。

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T48/T48n2003.xml). Blue Cliff Record by Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo. Original speaker: Fushan Fayuan; later commentator: Yuanwu Keqin. Yuanwu quotes Fushan's paired rule, then applies it to Yunmen's heirs and Baling's answer about the hair-blowing sword.

Senses.Explanation: Fushan's pair reverses the priority between a saying's wording and its intent according to whether the person has broken through. Yuanwu Keqin quotes Fushan Fayuan: one who has not penetrated does better to investigate the intent than the phrase, while one who has penetrated does better to investigate the phrase than the intent. Yuanwu then uses that distinction to compare answers by Yunmen's heirs, judging Baling's line about the hair-blowing sword as obtaining the phrase. The saying therefore does not discard words in favor of a hidden meaning; it makes phrase and intent answer to different conditions and restores close attention to the phrase after penetration.

Entries.SourceTerm: 未達境惟心，起種種分別

Senses.PreferredTarget: Failing to see that appearances are mind, one gives rise to many distinctions
SearchAliases: failing to see that appearances are mind, one gives rise to many distinctions
Senses.Note: The verse says that failure to see appearances as mind gives rise to many distinctions. Baichi asks whether the hall, sky, and ground can simply be called mind. Jiqi raises a whisk and asks whether calling it a whisk separates or covers it. Miyin places the line in a sermon on mind and circumstances. Chulin points to his staff and asks if mind and what appears are one or different. Yushan turns to wind, dust, birds, and flowers. The line opens a test that naming alone cannot settle.

Senses.Explanation: The first half of the fixed birth couplet: before leaving Tushita, already descended to the royal palace. Liao'an Qingyu sets the half at the hall seat and gives Shakyamuni, the founder, and the robe-seeking monk each a not-a-cheep before the staff strikes once, Qianyan Yuanzhang gives it his own verse, the sun's rise delighting the sky and the clouds' rise grieving the earth, asking only how one could stay unaged like the ever-flowing water, Yichu Wuyuan holds that whoever knows where the answer lands sees Shakyamuni in the couplet, else the Yunmen master's killing blow buys the world its peace, and Miyun Yuanwu voices it at the layman's birthday, asking whom it saves at just that time and leaving each to wake on their own before the staff falls. Shiyu Mingfang faults the descent and the birth each as a blush of shame and prefers Old Zhang of the east village and Black Li of the west, following the stream at dawn and treading white clouds home, Tianran Hanshi presses at the bath of the Buddha whether King Suddhodana's palace ever held the crown prince and who then was teaching in Tushita, then strikes the staff once and tells them this is not theirs to understand, and Yushan Shangsi rules the jujube-cypress master sharp only at the awl's point and blind to the chisel's square, reading the crown prince as the one who shed the jeweled robe for the patched one and waded into mud and water for people.

Senses.Explanation: Take it crosswise and use it upside down describes handling something without keeping to its ordinary orientation. Senses.Explanation: To speak across and upright is to speak at length in every direction or manner. Chan records use the paired verbs to characterize extensive discourse, sometimes adding contrary or compliant speech, and then appraise what such speech does not reach. Huangbo Xiyun says Niutou spoke every which way but still did not know the upward hinge. Chijue Daochong describes Shakyamuni speaking every which way through hundreds of assemblies and still not reaching the matter. Wuyi Yuanlai repeats the phrase for Shakyamuni and for his own present address, adding contrary and compliant speech. Tianyi Yihuai says an unnamed questioning monk may speak every which way yet still lack the eye at the crown. These uses characterize discourse range; they do not establish a separate thing for each direction.

Senses.Explanation: “Vast, boundless surging waves” pictures an immense expanse of turbulent water through which movement or communication is difficult. Yuanwu Keqin intensifies the image with white waves towering to the sky. Tianjie Min independently says communication is difficult across the vast waves. Miyun casts the vast waves as the field for fishing in his own opening verse and asks the assembly to meet the leaping fish. Sanyi describes the vast eastern sea in his own bell-board address before turning the image toward recognizing the source. Tianyin describes Sudhana in vast waves in his own praise of a Guanyin painting. Yingning comments that the seeker falls into the vast waves and a fishermans hand in his own case interpretation.

Senses.Explanation: "Vast waves stretch into the distance; white breakers surge to the sky" sets an overwhelming sea before the listener. In these four records the same complete image serves as a hall challenge, memorial turn, scripture image, and direct reply. Qianyan makes the sea a situation requiring rescue. Buhui uses it to open a memorial turn. Zizhou uses the vast waves for the reach of scriptures; Qiran gives the whole pair to a monk asking for a release line.

Senses.PreferredTarget: the school's interview claws and fangs
AlternateTargets: sharp interview moves
the school's pressing and releasing moves
Senses.Explanation: The school's interview claws and fangs are its sharp moves of pressing, releasing, seizing, and testing in public exchange. Qianyan Yuanzhang explicitly says that one press and one squeeze, one release and one taking-away are called the school's claws and fangs and also its handle. Xueguan Zhiyin appraises Huangbo Xiyun's calling and questioning of Pei Xiu as skillful use of them. Tianyin Yuanxiu contrasts two elders who expose them without harm with contemporaries who injure their own edge and hand. Feiyin Tongrong directs beginners who wish to disclose the inherited claws and fangs to question the new head monk. Qianyan also rejects several candidates that each claim the title but remain within the four propositions. The record therefore defines a public-interview family and tests its use rather than praising every sharp answer automatically.
Senses.Note: Five anchors across four independent records establish the Zen-loaded interview referent. It is distinct from people called the school's claws and fangs and from animal anatomy.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB444.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhuofeng Jue (卓峰玨禪師語錄). Chaoyuan Danya calls Zhuofeng Jue an outstanding figure of the teaching cavern and the school's claws and fangs.

Senses.PreferredTarget: an animal's claws and fangs
AlternateTargets: claws and teeth
predatory claws and fangs
Senses.Explanation: Claws and fangs also denote the concrete anatomy of a predatory animal. Foguo's address pictures a sleeping tiger's claws and fangs hidden in a cold crag and secluded valley. Jie Weizhou's verse pictures a hungry tiger suddenly opening its claws and fangs. Sleeping, hiding, hunger, and opening belong to the animal image rather than to a person-epithet or interview moves.
Senses.Note: Two independent records establish the anatomical animal referent.
